# cato_terminal_server_section (Resource)

Manages a custom section in the Cato terminal server (App & Data Inline Protection) policy. Adding a section can reassign existing rules into that section and create a draft revision; see provider documentation. Underlying GraphQL is marked @beta.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    cato = { source = "catonetworks/cato" }
  }
}

variable "token" {
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  description = "API token supplied through TF_VAR_token."
}

variable "account_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "Cato account ID supplied through TF_VAR_account_id."
}

provider "cato" {
  token      = var.token
  account_id = var.account_id
}

# Changes are automatically published. Use a test account when evaluating beta APIs.
resource "cato_terminal_server_section" "example" {
  at = {
    position = "LAST_IN_POLICY"
    # ref = "reference-section-id"
  }
  section = {
    name = "terraform-terminal-server-section"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `at` (Attributes) Where to insert the section (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--at))
- `section` (Attributes) Section name and computed ID (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--section))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Section ID

<a id="nestedatt--at"></a>
### Nested Schema for `at`

Required:

- `position` (String) Position relative to policy or another section

Optional:

- `ref` (String) Reference section ID when position is AFTER_SECTION or BEFORE_SECTION


<a id="nestedatt--section"></a>
### Nested Schema for `section`

Required:

- `name` (String) Section name

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Section ID

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/sh
terraform import cato_terminal_server_section.example "resource-id"
```
